Finding submitted: **compliant (sits at the fallback)**.

Summary of the review:
- **Vendor-side ownership is limited to its own IP** — Section 2.1(e) and 11.1(b) leave Array with its pre-existing Patents/Know-How only.
- **Our durable licence** — Section 13.1 converts the Section 2.1 grants into perpetual, irrevocable, fully paid-up, royalty-free, sublicensable licences, satisfying the fallback licence elements in substance.
- **We keep what we put in** — Ono owns its sole inventions (11.1(a)), INDs, Marketing Approvals and regulatory submissions (4.2(b)–(c)), and Patient Samples/Data (4.10); the 2.6 grant-back is a non-exclusive royalty-free licence subject to our exclusive rights, and Array's use of Ono Know-How is bounded to the Product.
- **Noted, not flagged** — joint ownership under 11.1(c)–(d) (mutual, and carved out for cross-licensed subject matter so we retain full exploitation in the Ono Territory), the territory limit and no-modification restriction (deal architecture), and Article XIV reversion (disapplied via 14.2(a)(ix) where we terminate for Array's breach). No assignment of our IP or Data to Array, so no walk-away trigger and no redline proposed.
